segments.text: a work in progress or whip limit is a
simple yet powerful tool that can
transform your workflow and enhance
productivity and efficiency imagine whip
limits as a stop sign for new work items
they ensure your team focuses on
finishing current work before starting
new ones by limiting the number of
things you're working on you can
actually get them done faster it's about
doing more by doing less but how to set
up your whip limits well there's no one
siiz fits approach but a good starting
point is the number of team members plus
one so for a team of five your whip
limit would be six however to really
leverage whip limits map out your
workflow on a combon board with a column
for each stage this way you can set whip
limits for each step of the process to
control the flow of work let's say you
have a team of seven three designers
three engineers and one QA so naturally
the whip limits will be three for
designers three for engineers and one
for QA and one extra which we will add
to the QA column as your workflow
evolves respect your limits and only
break them with good
reason remember processes become more
complex over time so consider adding
active and Q columns to your combon
board Q columns show where work items
are waiting to be pulled into the active
stage this helps you identify and
address bottlenecks even faster monitor
your team's workflow regularly and limit
your Q columns as well to ensure a
smooth workflow whip limits make it easy
to see your team's capacity identify
potential roadblocks adjust resources as
needed and ultimately deliver value
faster consider using digital tools like
business map to easily apply whip limits
to your workflow boost team efficiency
and get more done
